descriptors.concept_name: Company Liquidation Dividend And Undistributed Assets Account [Section 352]
descriptors.definition: Liquidators must deposit unpaid creditor dividends and refundable contributory assets remaining undistributed for six months into a designated special account maintained with a scheduled bank. Upon company dissolution, all remaining balances of unpaid dividends or undistributed assets must similarly be transferred to this account alongside a detailed statement furnished to the Registrar.
terminology: Company Liquidation Dividend and Undistributed Assets Account
inclusion: Dividends payable to creditors remaining unpaid for six months
Assets refundable to contributories remaining undistributed for six months
Any money in the liquidator's hands at the date of company dissolution
exclusion: Funds distributed within the statutory six-month window
General operational funds of the company prior to winding up
nearby_distinctions: Differs from general company bank accounts by being a dedicated statutory repository managed under regulatory oversight for unclaimed liquidation proceeds.

descriptors.definition: If a liquidator defaults on filing returns, accounts, or notices and fails to rectify the default within fourteen days of service of notice, the Tribunal may order compliance at the liquidator's personal cost. This remedial power is without prejudice to any other statutory penalties applicable to the defaulting liquidator.
inclusion: Orders directing liquidators to make good procedural defaults within a specified time
Imposition of costs incidental to the application upon the liquidator
exclusion: Substantive asset distribution disputes unrelated to statutory filing defaults
nearby_distinctions: Focuses specifically on enforcing procedural filing and notification compliance rather than general asset management or distribution.

descriptors.concept_name: Meetings To Ascertain Wishes Of Creditors Or Contributories [Section 354]
descriptors.definition: The Tribunal may direct meetings of creditors or contributories to be held under an appointed chairman to ascertain their collective wishes regarding winding up matters. Weight is assigned based on the financial value of each creditor's debt and the voting count held by each contributory.
inclusion: Tribunal directed meetings to gauge stakeholder consensus
Evaluation weighted by debt value for creditors and voting rights for contributories
exclusion: Binding judicial adjudications that override creditor or contributory preferences
nearby_distinctions: Serves as an advisory mechanism for the Tribunal to gauge stakeholder sentiment rather than a definitive voting decree.

descriptors.concept_name: Court, Tribunal Or Person, Etc., Before Whom Affidavit May Be Sworn [Section 355]
descriptors.definition: Affidavits required under the winding up chapter may be sworn in India before any authorized court, tribunal, judge, or person, and in foreign countries before authorized foreign authorities or Indian diplomatic and consular officers. Indian judicial authorities must take judicial notice of the official seals, stamps, and signatures affixed to these documents.
inclusion: Affidavits sworn before authorized domestic judicial officers
Affidavits sworn before foreign courts or Indian diplomatic officers abroad
exclusion: Unauthenticated statements lacking required official seals or signatures
nearby_distinctions: Specifically governs the formal execution and cross-jurisdictional acceptance of evidentiary affidavits for winding up proceedings.

descriptors.concept_name: Powers Of Tribunal To Declare Dissolution Of Company Void [Section 356]
descriptors.definition: Within two years of a company's dissolution, the Tribunal may declare the dissolution void upon application by the liquidator or an interested person, allowing winding up proceedings to resume as if dissolution had not occurred. Certified copies of this order must be filed with the Registrar within specified timelines.
inclusion: Applications filed within two years of dissolution
Orders restoring the legal existence of a dissolved company for ongoing proceedings
exclusion: Applications filed after the expiry of the two-year statutory window
nearby_distinctions: Reverses a finalized corporate dissolution to handle residual matters, distinct from initial winding up orders.

descriptors.concept_name: Commencement Of Winding Up By Tribunal [Section 357]
descriptors.definition: The official winding up of a company by the Tribunal is legally deemed to commence retrospectively at the exact time when the winding up petition was initially presented. This statutory marker establishes the temporal baseline for subsequent legal calculations and protective measures.
inclusion: Timeline determination anchored to the petition presentation date
exclusion: The date of the actual winding up order passed by the Tribunal
nearby_distinctions: Marks the inception point of winding up based on petition filing rather than the subsequent date of formal order issuance.

descriptors.concept_name: Exclusion Of Certain Time In Computing Period Of Limitation [Section 358]
descriptors.definition: When computing limitation periods for suits or applications filed by or on behalf of a company in tribunal winding up, a specific timeframe is excluded. This exclusion covers the duration from the commencement of winding up until one year immediately following the winding up order.
inclusion: Time span from winding up commencement to one year post-order for limitation computations
exclusion: Standard limitation periods running outside the protected winding up window
nearby_distinctions: Provides a statutory buffer specifically for corporate litigation limitation periods during active tribunal winding up proceedings.
